explanation: Cosine similarity is the normalized dot product, so it keeps the angle and drops the length of each document. Euclidean distance is the straight-line L2 length of the difference, and Manhattan distance is the sum of absolute coordinate differences; both still grow when one document is a longer copy of the other. Mahalanobis distance is the square root of (x−μ)ᵀΣ⁻¹(x−μ) (that expression itself is the squared distance), which rescales by a covariance once you have one, and it is not the bag-of-words angle.
